Defence Holdings Plc - Second UK Government Contract

LONDON, United Kingdom, September 18
18 September 2026
Defence Holdings Secures Second UK Government Contract, Advancing Commercial Execution
Defence Holdings PLC (LSE: ALRT)
, the UK's software-led defence technology group, today announces that it has secured its second customer contract with the UK Government, following completion of the contracting process referenced in the Company's previous updates to the market.
The contract represents the Company's second customer engagement with the UK Government in recent months and marks further progress in the commercial execution of the Defence Holdings Operating Model.
Highlights
·
Second customer contract secured with the UK Government
·
Initial six-month pilot commencing immediately
·
Engagement structured similarly to the Company's first UK Government contract
·
Defence Holdings will work directly with customer stakeholders throughout the initial pilot period
·
Contract represents further progress in translating customer engagement into contracted delivery
Second UK Government Contract
The Company has now completed the contracting process in relation to the second UK Government customer engagement referenced in its previous updates to the market.
The engagement will comprise an initial six-month pilot, structured similarly to the Company's first UK Government engagement. Delivery will commence immediately, with Defence Holdings working directly with customer stakeholders throughout the initial pilot period.
Due to the confidential and security-sensitive nature of the engagement, there are limitations on the information the Company is able to share with the market at this time. Accordingly, the Company is unable to disclose the specific customer requirements, operational application, commercial value or other sensitive details relating to the engagement.
Strategic Importance
The award represents further progress in Defence Holdings' transition from capability development into customer delivery and provides the Company with a second opportunity to work directly alongside UK Government stakeholders against defined customer requirements.
The Company's approach is centred on developing sovereign software capabilities directly alongside customers, enabling technologies to be shaped against real-world requirements and providing a pathway from initial development and testing towards wider operational adoption.
The addition of a second UK Government customer engagement provides further evidence of the Company's ability to translate its technology capabilities and customer relationships into contracted activity.
Operating Model Execution
The contract represents another important step in the execution of the Defence Holdings Operating Model and builds on the commercial progress demonstrated through the Company's first UK Government engagement.
Understanding the sovereign defence technology ecosystem in the UK allows us to identify the highest potential investment portfolio at the same time as building products that address customers' problems that have not yet been solved. This will also allow us to build a diversified portfolio of equity and revenue.
With two revenue-bearing UK G
overnment customer engagements now secured, the Company is increasing the level of contracted delivery across the Group whilst continuing to develop its sovereign software capabilities directly alongside end users.
The Board believes this approach provides Defence Holdings with a clear pathway to accelerate capability maturity, deepen customer relationships and progress technologies from development into operational and commercial adoption.
Andrew Roughan, CEO of Defence Holdings, commented:
"Securing our second contract with the UK Government represents another important step in the execution of our strategy and demonstrates continued progress in converting customer engagement into contracted activity.
"Our approach is built around working directly with customers to understand their requirements and develop sovereign software capabilities against real-world need. This second engagement gives us another opportunity to do exactly that, working alongside customer stakeholders throughout the initial pilot period.
"With two UK Government customer engagements now secured, we are continuing to build the commercial foundations of Defence Holdings whilst ensuring our technology roadmap remains closely aligned to evolving customer requirements."
About Defence Holdings PLC (ALRT)
Defence Holdings PLC (LSE: ALRT) is the UK's first listed software-led defence company. Its five-year strategic plan focuses on delivering sovereign digital capabilities across national security, resilience, and defence readiness.

10 September 2026
London, UK
Defence Holdings Provides Operational and Strategic Business Update
Defence Holdings PLC (LSE: ALRT), the UK's software-led defence technology group, today provides investors and shareholders with an operational update ahead of the Company's Annual General Meeting on 22 September 2026, providing further detail on the continued execution of its Operating Model through updates on ongoing project delivery, commercial contracts, the development of its sovereign software capabilities and product ecosystem, and the expansion of its Investment Pillar. Operational updates of this nature will now be delivered on a quarterly basis.
Highlights
● First UK Ministry of Defence contract continues to progress through delivery, with three priority use cases identified and completion remaining on track for October 2026.
● Second UK Ministry of Defence customer engagement has advanced materially, with contracting discussions progressing and the Company continuing to expect the contract to be secured in the near term.
● Sovereign software product ecosystem expands further, with the Company's fourth and fifth products now in active development following the identification of additional customer problem sets.
● Defence Fund investment pipeline expands to nine opportunities, with three having progressed to an advanced stage of discussion and engagement with prospective third-party investors.
● Defence Holdings and Whitespace to mark twelve months of their strategic partnership, with a recorded discussion between the companies' Chief Executives to be published on 15 September 2026.
Operational Update
This operational update comes at a time when Defence Holdings is making significant progress in the execution of its Operating Model across multiple strategic activities. In recent weeks, the Company announced the activation of the Investment Pillar of its Operating Model through the launch of the Defence Fund and, earlier this week, the formal commencement of the Meridian Accelerator Programme, introducing the ten companies selected for its inaugural cohort and the technologies and customer problem sets they have the potential to address across UK Defence.
Alongside these developments, the Company has continued to make progress across its commercial activities, including the active delivery of its first UK Ministry of Defence contract under Project Strong, the progression of a second anticipated Ministry of Defence engagement and the continued development of its broader commercial pipeline. The following update provides investors and shareholders with further detail on these activities, together with progress across the Company's sovereign software capabilities, strategic investment activities and defence technology ecosystem, ahead of its Annual General Meeting on 22 September 2026.
Customer & Commercial Update
First UK Ministry of Defence Contract
Delivery of the Company's first UK Ministry of Defence contract continues to advance, with the programme remaining on track for completion in October 2026.
Three priority use cases have now been identified in collaboration with the customer, with delivery progressing through a series of agile development sprints. Relevant end-user groups are actively engaged in developing representative operational scenarios, which are being incorporated into the capability to assess performance against each use case and inform further development and refinement.
This next phase of delivery will provide further validation of the capability against identified customer requirements ahead of the scheduled completion of the initial pilot in October.
Second UK Government Contract
The Company continues to progress contracting discussions in relation to the second customer engagement with the UK Government referenced in its previous updates to the market.
These discussions have advanced materially since the Company's last update and there has been no change to the anticipated scope or structure of the engagement. The Company continues to expect the contract to be secured in the near term.
The proposed engagement is expected to comprise an initial four-month pilot, structured similarly to the Company's first UK Ministry of Defence engagement. Subject to completion of the contracting process, delivery is expected to commence immediately thereafter, with the Company working directly with customer stakeholders through the initial pilot period.
Commercial Pipeline
Alongside its existing customer delivery activities, the Company is actively developing a broader pipeline of commercial opportunities across UK Defence and allied markets.
Within the UK Ministry of Defence, Defence Holdings is working across a broader range of stakeholders to identify opportunities for further design partnerships, applying the customer-led approach established through Project Strong to additional operational requirements and capability

8 September 2026
London, UK
Defence Holdings Announces Inaugural Meridian Cohort
Defence Holdings PLC ("Defence Holdings", "DH" or the "Company"), the UK-based defence technology company focused on delivering sovereign software capabilities for the UK and its allies, is pleased to announce the ten companies selected to participate in the inaugural cohort of Meridian, the Company's defence technology accelerator programme.
The inaugural cohort brings into the Defence Holdings ecosystem a new range of technologies and capabilities addressing identified requirements across defence and national security. Through Meridian, the Company will work alongside each cohort member to accelerate the development of these capabilities, strengthen their connection to operational requirements and create clearer pathways towards customers, deployment and commercial opportunities.
The programme formally commenced on 1 September 2026 and is now in active delivery with its inaugural cohort.
Highlights
●
Ten companies selected to participate in Meridian's inaugural cohort, bringing a broad range of technologies and capabilities addressing identified requirements across defence and national security into the Defence Holdings ecosystem.
●
Cohort combines emerging technologies with existing commercial and operational traction, including UK Ministry of Defence contracts, NATO and allied defence deployments, established commercial revenues and customer pipelines.
●
Selected companies span areas of growing strategic importance including autonomous systems, resilient communications, AI assurance, intelligence, information warfare, electronic warfare, maritime security and critical infrastructure protection, with several of these areas receiving significant UK Government defence investment.
●
Meridian provides Defence Holdings with earlier and deeper access to emerging defence technologies, creating opportunities for collaboration, technology integration, joint customer engagement, commercial partnerships and, where appropriate, strategic investment.
●
Meridian formally commenced on 1 September 2026 and is now in active delivery, with initial deep-dive sessions underway and individual technical, commercial and customer roadmaps being developed for each cohort member.
Selection of the Inaugural Cohort
The selection process for Meridian's inaugural cohort attracted an exceptionally strong response from across the UK technology ecosystem, both in the volume of applications received and the quality of the businesses and technologies represented. Applications spanned a broad range of capabilities relevant to defence and national security, creating a highly competitive selection process for the ten companies ultimately chosen to form the inaugural cohort.
Applications were reviewed through a structured selection process led by Defence Holdings PLC, with the selection committee comprising members of the Company's broader team together with representatives from Meridian's partner ecosystem, including Oracle and IMSL.The composition of the committee ensured that each application was assessed from multiple perspectives, combining technical scrutiny with an understanding of operational defence requirements, commercial potential and the practical pathways required to move emerging technologies towards deployment.
Companies were assessed against a range of criteria, including the relevance of their technology to identifiable defence and national security problem sets, technical differentiation and maturity, potential pathways towards operational deployment, scalability, sovereign capability and the strength of the team responsible for its development. Particular emphasis was placed on technologies where Meridian's combination of defence relationships, technical expertise and strategic partners could provide a meaningful opportunity to accelerate progress.
The ten companies ultimately selected bring together a diverse range of technologies and capabilities aligned to areas of growing importance across defence and national security. The cohort combines emerging technologies with businesses already demonstrating commercial and operational traction, including UK Ministry of Defence contracts, NATO and allied defence deployments, established commercial revenues and customer pipelines. Collectively, they reflect Meridian's focus on identifying technologies with clear relevance to current and emerging operational requirements, together with a credible pathway towards practical application and commercial adoption.
Inaugural Cohort Members
A short overview of each of the ten companies selected for Meridian's inaugural cohort is provided below in alphabetical order. Further information on each cohort member can be found at
meridianbydefenceplc.com
.

Defence Holdings Publishes Open Letter to Shareholders Following Cornerstone Investment in Defence Fund
19
August 2026. Defence Holdings PLC (LSE: ALRT) ("Defence Holdings", the "Company" or the "Group") the UK software-led defence technology group, announces that its Chief Executive Officer, Andrew Roughan, has today published an Open Letter to Shareholders.
The letter provides additional context to the Company's announcement on 17 August 2026 regarding its £2 million cornerstone investment in the Defence Fund,
marking the activation of the Investment Pillar of the Defence Holdings Playbook first outlined in May 2026
.
In the letter, Mr Roughan expands on the strategic rationale for the investment, how it aligns with the Company's previously communicated five-pillar operating model, the reasons for establishing the Fund through a separate investment vehicle, the governance arrangements surrounding the Fund and the protections established for Defence Holdings and its shareholders.
The letter explains how the cornerstone investment aligns with the Company's long-term strategy and capital allocation framework, confirms that it is fully funded from existing resources and provides further context on the Board's approach to capital deployment.
The publication of today's letter forms part of Andrew Roughan's commitment, first articulated upon his appointment as Chief Executive Officer, to maintaining open, transparent and accessible communication with shareholders as Defence Holdings executes its long-term strategy.
The Company also announces that Mr Roughan will participate in a longer-form interview later this week, discussing the Defence Fund and a number of related strategic themes in greater detail. Further information regarding the timing and publication of that interview will be announced in due course.
The full text of the Open Letter from the Chief Executive Officer follows below, and can be accessed online at:
www.defenceplc.com/news-room/
OPEN LETTER TO SHAREHOLDERS
Dear Shareholders,
Yesterday's announcement regarding Defence Holdings' cornerstone investment in the Defence Fund generated significant discussion amongst investors. I have followed that discussion closely and wanted to take the opportunity to provide some additional colour and context around how this investment fits within our long-term strategy, and to address a number of the key themes that have emerged since.
The Strategy in Context
When I joined Defence Holdings, I committed to building a business capable of creating significant long-term shareholder value through an integrated model built on five connected pillars announced in our Playbook in May: Accelerator, Investment, Product, Commercial Channel, and Technology Channel.
This means building a business that can generate profitable contracts
and
taking equity positions in high-potential companies that our model can support to a more successful outcome. The combination of revenue that drives profit and an equity portfolio is my planned value creation model.
Since May, we've made meaningful progress across each:
● Secured our first customer contract with the UK Ministry of Defence
● Launched Meridian with our inaugural cohort beginning soon
● Activated the Investment pillar through the Defence Fund
These aren't isolated announcements, they are deliberate milestones against the strategy I committed to delivering.
Addressing Your Questions
On Capital Deployment
The June fundraising was designed to execute this strategy. The £2 million cornerstone investment into the Fund forms part of that plan. It is not capital diverted from operations; it is capital strengthening the ecosystem that supports our business.
Structurally, because the Fund is a managed Alternative Investment Fund, investors (including Defence Holdings) get a direct, look-through economic interest in the underlying portfolio companies, so there is no material economic difference between Defence Holdings investing in a target company directly or via the Fund. What the Fund route adds is the ability to share risk and capital with other professional investors, giving access to more and potentially larger opportunities than Defence Holdings' own balance sheet could support alone, without concentrating Defence Holdings' capital in any single early-stage position.
To be clear: this investment does not signal that Defence Holdings will require additional equity funding for working capital.
Why Not Manage the Fund Ourselves?
It's a fair question. The answer comes down to two things: scale and structure.
The sovereign defence technology opportunity is uniquely large. Meaningful participation requires access to substantially more capital than our balance sheet could reasonably deploy.
